opførsel.explanation: "Opførsel" means "behavior". To say someone behaves badly, use "dårlig opførsel" (bad behavior): "Dårlig opførsel er ikke tilladt" (Bad behavior is not allowed). To talk about manners, use "manerer" (manners): "gode manerer" (good manners).

ophidset.explanation: "Ophidset" means "agitated". To describe a heated argument, use it before the noun: "en ophidset debat" (a heated debate). It can also mean sexually aroused.

opkast.explanation: "Opkast" means "vomit". It is built from "op" (up) and "et kast" (a throw), like the verb "at kaste op" (to throw up). To say a child is throwing up, use the verb: "Barnet kaster op" (The child is throwing up).

opladning.explanation: "Opladning" means "charging". It comes from the verb "at oplade" (to charge). To say you charge a phone, use the verb: "Jeg lader telefonen op" (I am charging the phone).

oplagt.explanation: "Oplagt" means "obvious". When you describe a person who is full of energy, it also means "in good form": "Hun er godt oplagt i dag" (She is in good form today).

opmærksom.explanation: "Opmærksom" means "attentive". To say you are aware of something, add "på" (on) after it: "Jeg er opmærksom på problemet" (I am aware of the problem).

opmærksom på.explanation: "Opmærksom på" means "aware of". To point something out to someone, use "at gøre nogen opmærksom på" (to make someone aware of): "Jeg gjorde ham opmærksom på fejlen" (I pointed out the mistake to him).

opmærksomhed.explanation: "Opmærksomhed" means "attention". It is the noun for the word "opmærksom" (attentive). To ask a room for its attention, say: "Må jeg bede om jeres opmærksomhed?" (May I have your attention?)

oppe.explanation: "Oppe" means "up". When something is already in a high place, use it: "Katten er oppe på bordet" (The cat is up on the table). When something moves up, use "op" (up) instead: "Katten hopper op på bordet" (The cat jumps up onto the table). To ask whether someone is out of bed, use it too: "Er du oppe?" (Are you up?)

oprevet.explanation: "Oprevet" means "upset". To say someone is upset after something unpleasant, use it with "efter" (after): "Hun var meget oprevet efter skænderiet" (She was very upset after the argument).

oprigtig.explanation: "Oprigtig" means "sincere". To give your honest opinion, use it before the noun: "Det er min oprigtige mening" (That is my sincere opinion). To tell someone to speak the truth, use "ærlig" (honest) instead: "Vær ærlig" (Be honest).

oprindelig.explanation: "Oprindelig" means "original". For something new and creative, use "original" instead: "en original idé" (an original idea). To say what was true at the start, use "oprindeligt" (originally): "Oprindeligt boede vi i Aarhus" (Originally we lived in Aarhus).

oprørsk.explanation: "Oprørsk" means "rebellious". It comes from the noun "et oprør" (a revolt). To describe a teenager who refuses to follow the rules: "en oprørsk teenager" (a rebellious teenager).

oprørt.explanation: "Oprørt" means "upset". It can also describe water: "et oprørt hav" (a rough sea). To say what upset someone, use "over" (about): "oprørt over nyheden" (upset about the news).

opsyn.explanation: "Opsyn" means "supervision". To say who is being watched over, use it with "under" (under): "Børnene er under opsyn" (The children are being supervised).

optaget.explanation: "Optaget" means "busy". When a seat or a table is in use, it means "taken": "Er denne plads optaget?" (Is this seat taken?) When a person has no time, it means "busy": "Jeg er optaget lige nu" (I am busy right now).

optimistisk.explanation: "Optimistisk" means "optimistic". It is the adjective for the noun "en optimist" (an optimist). To say you are cautiously optimistic: "Jeg er forsigtigt optimistisk" (I am cautiously optimistic).

opvaskemiddel.explanation: "Opvaskemiddel" means "dish soap". It is built from "at vaske op" (to wash dishes) and "et middel" (a product). For clothes, use "vaskepulver" (laundry detergent) instead: "Jeg køber vaskepulver" (I buy laundry detergent).

orange.explanation: "Orange" means "orange", as in the color. For the fruit, use "en appelsin" (an orange): "Jeg spiser en appelsin" (I am eating an orange).

ordblind.explanation: "Ordblind" means "dyslexic". It is built from "ord" (word) and "blind" (blind), so it is literally "word-blind".

ordentlig.explanation: "Ordentlig" means "proper". When you describe a person, it means "decent": "en ordentlig mand" (a decent man). To say how something is done, use "ordentligt" (properly): "Gør det ordentligt" (Do it properly).

organiseret.explanation: "Organiseret" means "organized". It comes from the verb "at organisere" (to organize). To say something is well organized, add "vel" (well) in front: "velorganiseret" (well organized).

original.explanation: "Original" means "original", as in the first version rather than a copy. For a creative, new idea, it has a second meaning: "en original idé" (an original idea).

os.explanation: "Os" means "us". When someone sees or helps us, use it: "Han ser os" (He sees us). When we are the ones doing the action, use "vi" (we): "Vi ser ham" (We see him).

ost.explanation: "Ost" means "cheese". To talk about one kind of cheese, put "en" before it: "en fransk ost" (a French cheese).

otte.explanation: "Otte" means "eight". To keep it apart from "atten" (eighteen), compare "otte børn" (eight children) and "atten børn" (eighteen children).

ottende.explanation: "Ottende" means "eighth". To say a date, put it before the month: "den ottende marts" (the eighth of March).

ovenover.explanation: "Ovenover" means "upstairs". To say where a noise comes from, use it after the verb: "Der er støj ovenover" (There is noise upstairs). To say the floor below instead, use "nedenunder" (downstairs): "Vi bor nedenunder" (We live downstairs).

ovenpå.explanation: "Ovenpå" means "upstairs". To ask where someone is in the house, use it after the verb: "Er børnene ovenpå?" (Are the children upstairs?) For the floor below, use "nedenunder" (downstairs): "Køkkenet er nedenunder" (The kitchen is downstairs).

over.explanation: "Over" means "over". To say something is higher than a place, use it before the place: "Flyet flyver over byen" (The plane flies over the city). To say you cross something, use it with a verb of moving: "Katten løber over vejen" (The cat runs across the road). To say more than a number, use it before the number: "Der kom over tyve mennesker" (More than twenty people came).

overalt.explanation: "Overalt" means "everywhere". It is built from "over" (over) and "alt" (all). It can also come first in the sentence: "Overalt er der blomster" (Everywhere there are flowers).

overarbejde.explanation: "Overarbejde" means "overtime". It is built from "over" (over) and "arbejde" (work). To say you work overtime, use "at arbejde over" (to work overtime): "Jeg arbejder over i dag" (I am working overtime today).

overbevisende.explanation: "Overbevisende" means "convincing". It comes from the verb "at overbevise" (to convince): "Han overbeviste mig" (He convinced me).

overdreven.explanation: "Overdreven" means "exaggerated". It comes from the verb "at overdrive" (to exaggerate). To say someone is far too polite, use it before the noun: "overdreven høflighed" (excessive politeness).

overfladisk.explanation: "Overfladisk" means "superficial". It comes from "en overflade" (a surface). To say someone knows little about a subject, use it before the noun: "overfladisk viden" (superficial knowledge). To describe a person, use it after "er" (is): "Han er meget overfladisk" (He is very superficial).

overfor.explanation: "Overfor" means "across from". To say you are facing a choice or problem, use "at stå overfor" (to be faced with): "Jeg står overfor et valg" (I am facing a choice).

overfyldt.explanation: "Overfyldt" means "overcrowded". It is built from "over" (too much) and "fyldt" (filled). To say a drawer has too much in it: "en overfyldt skuffe" (an overfull drawer).

overhovedet.explanation: "Overhovedet" means "at all". To say not at all, put it before "ikke" (not): "Jeg forstår overhovedet ikke" (I do not understand at all).

overlegen.explanation: "Overlegen" means "commanding". To say a team is clearly better than its opponents, it means "superior": "Holdet var overlegen" (The team was superior). To describe a person who looks down on others: "Han talte med en overlegen tone" (He spoke in a superior tone).

overlevelse.explanation: "Overlevelse" means "survival". It comes from the verb "at overleve" (to survive): "Vi overlevede" (We survived).

overmodig.explanation: "Overmodig" means "overconfident". It is built from "over" (too much) and "mod" (courage), so it is courage that has gone too far. To tell someone to be careful: "Vær ikke så overmodig" (Do not be so overconfident).

overordnet.explanation: "Overordnet" means "overall". To say broadly speaking, use "overordnet set" (broadly speaking): "Overordnet set er planen god" (Broadly speaking, the plan is good).

overraskende.explanation: "Overraskende" means "surprising". To say how you feel yourself, use "overrasket" (surprised): "Jeg er overrasket" (I am surprised).

overskuelig.explanation: "Overskuelig" means "clear". To say a task is small enough to handle, it means "manageable": "Opgaven er overskuelig" (The task is manageable). The opposite is "uoverskuelig" (impossible to get an overview of): "Situationen er uoverskuelig" (The situation is impossible to get an overview of).

overskyet.explanation: "Overskyet" means "overcast". It comes from "en sky" (a cloud). To say what the weather is like: "Det er overskyet" (It is overcast).

overvågning.explanation: "Overvågning" means "surveillance". It comes from the verb "at overvåge" (to monitor). In a hospital, it can mean watching over a patient: "overvågning af patienten" (monitoring of the patient).

overvægt.explanation: "Overvægt" means "overweight". To say a person is overweight, use it with "at have" (to have): "Han har overvægt" (He is overweight). At the airport, it means baggage over the weight limit: "Kufferten har overvægt" (The suitcase is overweight).

overvældende.explanation: "Overvældende" means "overwhelming". To describe a task that is too big, use it before the noun: "en overvældende opgave" (an overwhelming task). To say how you feel yourself, use "overvældet" (overwhelmed): "Jeg er overvældet" (I am overwhelmed).

overvældet.explanation: "Overvældet" means "overwhelmed". To say how you feel: "Jeg er overvældet" (I am overwhelmed). To describe the thing that overwhelms you, use "overvældende" (overwhelming): "en overvældende opgave" (an overwhelming task).

at ødelægge.explanation: "At ødelægge" means "to destroy / break". To say you broke your own phone: "Jeg ødelagde min telefon" (I broke my phone). To say a thing broke without anyone doing it, use "at gå i stykker" (to break): "Telefonen gik i stykker" (The phone broke).

at øge.explanation: "At øge" means "to increase". To say you make something bigger yourself, use it with the thing: "Vi øger farten" (We increase the speed). When something goes up by itself, use "at stige" (to rise): "Prisen stiger" (The price is rising).

at ønske.explanation: "At ønske" means "to wish". To wish someone something, put the person after the verb: "Jeg ønsker dig en god tur" (I wish you a good trip). To wish for something for yourself, add "sig" (oneself): "Jeg ønsker mig en cykel" (I wish for a bike).

at ønske sig.explanation: "At ønske sig" means "to wish for". To say what you want to get, use it with the thing: "Jeg ønsker mig en cykel" (I wish for a bike). To wish something to another person, leave out "sig" and use "at ønske" (to wish): "Jeg ønsker dig held og lykke" (I wish you good luck).

at øse.explanation: "At øse" means "to scoop / pour". To say you bail water out of a boat: "at øse vand ud af båden" (to bail water out of the boat). To say it is raining very hard, use it with "ned" (down): "Det øser ned!" (It is pouring down!)

at øve.explanation: "At øve" means "to practice". To say you practice yourself, add "mig" (myself): "Jeg øver mig i dansk" (I am practicing Danish). To say you rehearse something, put it right after the verb: "Børnene øver en sang" (The children are rehearsing a song).

at øve sig.explanation: "At øve sig" means "to practice". To say you practice, use "mig" (myself): "Jeg øver mig hver dag" (I practice every day). To say he or she practices, use "sig" (himself, herself): "Hun øver sig på klaveret" (She practices on the piano).

en ø.explanation: "En ø" means "an island". In Denmark, Copenhagen lies on the island "Sjælland" (Zealand).

en øjenfarve.explanation: "En øjenfarve" means "an eye color". To ask someone's eye color: "Hvad er din øjenfarve?" (What is your eye color?) To answer: "Jeg har brune øjne" (I have brown eyes).

en øjenlæge.explanation: "En øjenlæge" means "an eye doctor". It is built from "et øje" (an eye) and "en læge" (a doctor). To get your sight tested at a shop, go to "en optiker" (an optician): "Jeg skal til optikeren" (I am going to the optician).

en øjenvippe.explanation: "En øjenvippe" means "an eyelash". To describe someone's eyelashes, use the plural: "Hun har lange øjenvipper" (She has long eyelashes).

en økonom.explanation: "En økonom" means "an economist". The subject is "økonomi" (economics): "Hun læser økonomi" (She studies economics).

en økonomi.explanation: "En økonomi" means "an economy". It also means a person's or a household's finances: "Vi har en stram økonomi" (Our finances are tight).

en økse.explanation: "En økse" means "an axe". To say you chop wood, use the verb "at hugge" (to chop): "Jeg hugger brænde" (I chop firewood).

en øl.explanation: "En øl" means "a beer". To order a certain size, put the size word between "en" and "øl": "en stor øl" (a large beer).

en ølflaske.explanation: "En ølflaske" means "a beer bottle". It is built from "en øl" (a beer) and "en flaske" (a bottle). To order a bottle of beer: "En flaske øl, tak" (A bottle of beer, please).

en ønskeseddel.explanation: "En ønskeseddel" means "a wish list". It is built from "at ønske" (to wish) and "en seddel" (a note). In other words, "seddel" means a banknote: "en hundredkroneseddel" (a hundred-krone banknote).

en ørering.explanation: "En ørering" means "an earring". It is built from "et øre" (an ear) and "en ring" (a ring). To talk about a matching set, say "et par øreringe" (a pair of earrings).

en ørken.explanation: "En ørken" means "a desert". To say where you are, use "i" (in) before the word: "Vi gik i ørkenen i tre dage" (We walked in the desert for three days).

en ørn.explanation: "En ørn" means "an eagle". An eagle that lives near the sea is "en havørn" (a sea eagle): "Vi så en havørn ved fjorden" (We saw a sea eagle by the fjord).

en ørred.explanation: "En ørred" means "a trout". A trout that lives in the sea is "en havørred" (a sea trout): "Han fangede en havørred" (He caught a sea trout).

en øse.explanation: "En øse" means "a ladle". To say you serve food with it, use "at øse op" (to scoop out): "Han øser maden op" (He scoops out the food).

en østers.explanation: "En østers" means "an oyster". Oysters from the fjord "Limfjorden" are called "limfjordsøsters" (Limfjord oysters).

en øvelse.explanation: "En øvelse" means "an exercise". It comes from the verb "at øve" (to practice). In sport or at the gym, it means one move of a workout: "Gør denne øvelse ti gange" (Do this exercise ten times).

et øje.explanation: "Et øje" means "an eye". To say you watch someone or something, use "at holde øje med" (to keep an eye on): "Jeg holder øje med børnene" (I keep an eye on the children).

et øjeblik.explanation: "Et øjeblik" means "a moment". It is built from "et øje" (an eye) and "et blik" (a glance). To say right now, use "i øjeblikket" (at the moment): "Jeg læser i øjeblikket" (I am reading right now).

et øjekast.explanation: "Et øjekast" means "a glance". It is built from "et øje" (an eye) and "et kast" (a throw), so it is a throw of the eyes. To say how something seems at first glance, use "ved første øjekast" (at first glance): "Ved første øjekast er det en god pris" (At first glance it is a good price).

et øjenbryn.explanation: "Et øjenbryn" means "an eyebrow". To say someone raises an eyebrow, use the verb "at løfte" (to lift): "Han løftede et øjenbryn" (He raised an eyebrow).

et øjenlåg.explanation: "Et øjenlåg" means "an eyelid". It is built from "et øje" (an eye) and "et låg" (a lid). In other words, "et låg" is also a lid on a pot: "et låg på en gryde" (a lid on a pot).

et økosystem.explanation: "Et økosystem" means "an ecosystem". It is built from "øko" (eco) and "et system" (a system). The same "øko" is in "økologisk" (organic): "økologiske æg" (organic eggs).

et ønske.explanation: "Et ønske" means "a wish". To say a wish came true, use "gå i opfyldelse" (to come true): "Mit ønske gik i opfyldelse" (My wish came true). The verb is "at ønske" (to wish): "Jeg ønsker dig held og lykke" (I wish you good luck).

et øre.explanation: "Et øre" means "an ear". It is also a small unit of money worth a hundredth of a krone. To say a price with it: "Mælken koster tre kroner og halvtreds øre" (The milk costs three kroner and fifty øre).

øde.explanation: "Øde" means "deserted". For a place that is just calm and peaceful, use "stille" (quiet) instead: "Byen er stille" (The town is quiet).

ødelagt.explanation: "Ødelagt" means "broken". It comes from the verb "at ødelægge" (to destroy). To say a day or a plan is ruined: "Dagen er ødelagt" (The day is ruined).

ødelæggelse.explanation: "Ødelæggelse" means "destruction". It comes from the verb "at ødelægge" (to destroy). To talk about the damage after a flood: "Oversvømmelsen efterlod store ødelæggelser" (The flood left great destruction).

ødelæggende.explanation: "Ødelæggende" means "destructive". It comes from the verb "at ødelægge" (to destroy). To describe a fire that does great damage: "en ødelæggende brand" (a destructive fire).

øjeblikkelig.explanation: "Øjeblikkelig" means "immediate". It is built from "et øjeblik" (a moment). To ask for help right away, use it before the noun: "øjeblikkelig hjælp" (immediate help). To say how someone acted, use "øjeblikkeligt" (immediately) after the verb: "Han svarede øjeblikkeligt" (He answered immediately).

øjeblikkeligt.explanation: "Øjeblikkeligt" means "immediately". To say how quickly a person acts, use it after the verb: "Han svarede øjeblikkeligt" (He answered immediately). Before a noun, use "øjeblikkelig" (immediate): "øjeblikkelig hjælp" (immediate help).

øjensynligt.explanation: "Øjensynligt" means "apparently". It contains "øje" (eye) and "syn" (sight). It can also come first in the sentence: "Øjensynligt er han træt" (Apparently he is tired).

økologisk.explanation: "Økologisk" means "organic". In Denmark, organic food in shops carries the red "Ø-mærket" (the organic mark). To talk about organic eggs, use the plural ending: "økologiske æg" (organic eggs).

økonomisk.explanation: "Økonomisk" means "economic". When you describe a car that costs little to run, it means "economical": "en økonomisk bil" (an economical car).

øm.explanation: "Øm" means "sore". To say a body part is sore when touched: "Min arm er øm" (My arm is sore). To say something hurts, use "at have ondt" (to hurt): "Jeg har ondt i armen" (My arm hurts).

ønskelig.explanation: "Ønskelig" means "desirable". It comes from the verb "at ønske" (to wish). To say it would be good if everyone comes: "Det er ønskeligt, at alle kommer" (It is desirable that everyone comes).

øreringe.explanation: "Øreringe" means "earring". It is the plural, used when you mean more than one: "Jeg køber to øreringe" (I am buying two earrings).

øst.explanation: "Øst" means "east". To name the eastern part of a region, put it before the name: "Østjylland" (eastern Jutland).

østersøen.explanation: "Østersøen" means "the Baltic Sea". The Danish island Bornholm lies in it: "Bornholm ligger i Østersøen" (Bornholm lies in the Baltic Sea).

østpå.explanation: "Østpå" means "east". It is built from "øst" (east) and "på" (on). To say where a place lies, use "øst for" (east of) instead: "København ligger øst for Roskilde" (Copenhagen is east of Roskilde).

øvelse gør mester.explanation: "Øvelse gør mester" means "Practice makes perfect". Literally, it says that exercise makes a "mester" (master).

øverst.explanation: "Øverst" means "at the top". The opposite is "nederst" (at the bottom): "Navnet står nederst på siden" (The name is at the bottom of the page).

en / et.explanation: "En / et" means "a". Each Danish word takes only one of them: "en bil" (a car) but "et hus" (a house). To stress the number one, add an accent: "Jeg har én bil" (I have one car).

at padle.explanation: "At padle" means "to paddle". The tool you paddle with is "en pagaj" (a paddle): "Jeg har glemt min pagaj" (I have forgotten my paddle). For rowing with oars, use "at ro" (to row) instead: "Vi roer over søen" (We row across the lake).
